# Two more differences

<!-- STEP id="transport" -->
## Carrying food and water

A tree and a rabbit must both carry food and water to every part of the body, and they have different tissues for this job. In plants, **xylem** carries water and minerals, and **phloem** carries food. In animals, blood carries food, water and other materials around the body.

<!-- STEP id="growth" -->
## Growing all life long

Plants and animals also grow in different ways, because their tissues for growth are different. A neem tree grows taller and thicker year after year, all its life. A rabbit grows until it is an adult, and then it stops getting bigger.

<!-- STEP id="four-differences" -->
## The four differences

| | Plants | Animals |
|---|---|---|
| Support | Most are fixed in one place; stiff cell walls keep them firm | Most can move; no cell wall, so cells change shape |
| Food | Make food by photosynthesis | Digest the food they eat |
| Carrying materials | Xylem carries water, phloem carries food | Blood carries materials |
| Growth | Keep growing all their life | Most stop getting bigger once adult |

**Plants and animals live different lives, so their tissues are different.**
